title: How AI feedback supports lesson planning in vocational teacher education: a longitudinal intervention study using an analytical AI platform
venue: Empirical Research in Vocational Education and Training
extended_summary:
This paper examines whether an analytical AI platform can support lesson planning in teacher education by providing individualized feedback on lesson plans. The authors focus on a practical problem in vocational teacher education: university instructors often cannot provide frequent, detailed, expert-level feedback on complex lesson plans, especially when students must incorporate multiple didactic principles and planning dimensions.

The intervention used an analytical AI system called EDDA, which classifies uploaded lesson plans and materials into a coding framework and returns expert-like feedback. Unlike generative AI chatbots, EDDA is designed for reproducible, criteria-based feedback grounded in pre-trained categories. In the study, students in a master's-level vocational business education course worked on lesson plans across a semester and received AI feedback, with optional human follow-up discussion. A control group in a comparable course received human feedback only. The study also tracked several meta-dimensions, including AI literacy, AI attitudes, digital competences, self-efficacy with digital technologies, and motivation.

The participants were master’s students in business education in Germany, organized into small groups, with data collected across two winter semesters. The paper reports that the AI-supported group often matched or exceeded the control group in some lesson-plan dimensions, especially certain sustainability-related and didactic aspects such as action orientation, relatedness, technology use, lesson structure, and learner engagement. However, the authors also found that simply using AI did not automatically improve AI literacy, attitudes, or motivation. They conclude that analytical AI can effectively supplement traditional feedback, but it should be embedded in a broader pedagogical framework and used cautiously because the system tended to underestimate performance in some categories.

identified_tools.name: GenAI (General)
identified_tools.description: A generic generative AI/LLM chatbot or assistant used for producing or providing feedback, without a specific named product.
identified_tools.use_case: The paper reviews prior generative-AI feedback research in teacher education and contrasts generative AI feedback risks with the analytical AI platform EDDA; no specific named generative product was studied in the intervention.

quality_tier_rationale: This is a longitudinal intervention study, but the AI system evaluated is an analytical AI platform (EDDA), not a generative AI product. Because the user’s topic is specifically generative AI evidence, the paper is only indirectly relevant and does not provide direct named-product evidence of GenAI use.
impact_tier_rationale: The paper reports a substantive intervention effect for the analytical platform on some lesson-planning dimensions, with one significant positive effect on SDG 15 and other positive effects on social competences and reflexivity. However, the findings are not about generative AI, so the impact for the requested GenAI evidence base is limited and indirect.
